The antenna system includes three drive assemblies configured to rotate or pivot different frame and support assemblies about three separate axes. These drive assemblies cooperate to provide multi-axis positioning of the antenna structure, allowing the system to orient an antenna accurately in a desired direction.

A primary antenna and a secondary antenna are mounted in a fixed relationship relative to the level frame assembly. Because both antennas are affixed relative to the same level frame assembly, movement of the frame assembly correspondingly changes the orientation of the antennas while maintaining their relative positions.

The system also includes a control unit that determines which antenna is to be used. The control unit selects either the primary antenna or the secondary antenna for operation, depending on the operating mode, signal requirements, target direction, or other system conditions.

To position the selected antenna, the control unit determines the position of the elevation frame assembly based on sensed motion about the three separate axes. Motion sensors, position sensors, or other feedback devices may provide information indicating rotation or pivoting about each axis. The control unit uses this information to calculate or estimate the current orientation of the elevation frame assembly.

Based on the selected antenna and the determined position of the elevation frame assembly, the control unit controls one or more of the drive assemblies to adjust the position of the selected antenna. By commanding the appropriate drive assemblies, the control unit rotates or pivots the relevant frame and support assemblies until the selected antenna is aligned with a desired pointing direction. This coordinated control enables accurate positioning of either the primary antenna or the secondary antenna within the antenna system.
outputs.L4:
An antenna system includes a mechanical support structure and a set of drive assemblies that allow one or more antennas to be accurately aimed. The system has a support frame, a level frame, and an elevation frame arranged so that each frame can move about a respective axis. A first drive assembly rotates the support frame about a first axis, a second drive assembly pivots or levels the level frame about a second axis, and a third drive assembly pivots the elevation frame about a third axis. Together, these three controlled movements provide multi-axis positioning of the antenna structure.

A primary antenna and a secondary antenna are mounted in relation to the level frame. The antennas may be oriented differently or used for different communication functions, frequency bands, or operating conditions. The elevation frame supports or influences the pointing direction of the active antenna, while the level frame provides a stabilized reference that helps maintain proper alignment as the system moves.

The antenna system also includes a control unit that supervises operation of the drive assemblies and manages selection between the primary and secondary antennas. The control unit receives motion or position information from one or more sensors capable of detecting movement about multiple axes. Using this sensed information, the control unit determines the current position of the elevation frame and calculates the adjustments needed to aim the selected antenna toward a desired target, such as a satellite, base station, or other communication point.

During operation, the control unit selects either the primary antenna or the secondary antenna for use. After selecting the active antenna, the control unit commands the first, second, and third drive assemblies to rotate or pivot the corresponding frames until the chosen antenna reaches the desired orientation. If the system experiences movement, vibration, tilt, or a change in platform attitude, the sensors detect the change and the control unit compensates by adjusting the drive assemblies. This allows the active antenna to remain accurately pointed even when the platform carrying the antenna system is moving.

The system therefore provides a controllable, multi-axis antenna mount capable of precise aiming and reliable switching between antennas. By combining frame movement, sensor feedback, and automated drive control, the antenna system can maintain alignment of the selected antenna and quickly reposition or switch antennas as operating requirements change.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article, and it helps us refer to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we mean any book, but when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

This simple word brings clarity to sentences. It helps identify people, places, objects, and ideas. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our daily experience, and we say “the teacher” when we are talking about a specific teacher.

Although “the” may seem unimportant, it is essential in English. Without it, sentences can sound incomplete or unclear. Its frequent use shows that even the smallest words can have great meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert these invention notes into formal patent language: three-axis antenna mount, first drive rotates vertical support relative to base, second drive pivots level frame, third drive pivots elevation frame, dual antennas, controller selects antenna and adjusts position from sensed axis motion.
counterfactuals.output:
Below is a formal patent-style conversion of the invention notes.

---

## Formal Patent Language

### Title  
**Three-Axis Antenna Mounting System with Selectable Dual Antennas and Motion-Responsive Position Control**

### Abstract  
An antenna mounting system includes a base, a vertical support rotatably coupled to the base, a level frame pivotably coupled to the vertical support, and an elevation frame pivotably coupled to the level frame. A first drive is configured to rotate the vertical support relative to the base about a first axis. A second drive is configured to pivot the level frame about a second axis. A third drive is configured to pivot the elevation frame about a third axis. First and second antennas are supported by the elevation frame or otherwise operatively coupled to the mounting system. A controller is configured to select one of the first and second antennas for operation and to control at least one of the first, second, and third drives based at least in part on sensed motion associated with one or more of the axes.

---

## Detailed Description

An antenna positioning apparatus may include a base configured for mounting to a vehicle, vessel, platform, structure, or other support. A vertical support is coupled to the base and is rotatable relative to the base about a generally vertical or azimuth axis. A first drive mechanism is operatively coupled between the base and the vertical support and is configured to rotate the vertical support relative to the base.

A level frame is pivotably coupled to the vertical support. The level frame may be pivotable about a generally horizontal or roll/leveling axis. A second drive mechanism is operatively coupled to the level frame and is configured to pivot the level frame relative to the vertical support. The level frame may thereby compensate for tilt, roll, or other angular displacement of the base or support platform.

An elevation frame is pivotably coupled to the level frame. The elevation frame may be pivotable about an elevation axis that is transverse to the axis of rotation of the vertical support and may also be transverse to the pivot axis of the level frame. A third drive mechanism is operatively coupled to the elevation frame and is configured to pivot the elevation frame relative to the level frame, thereby adjusting an elevation angle of one or more antennas supported by the elevation frame.

In some embodiments, the apparatus includes a first antenna and a second antenna. The first and second antennas may be mounted to the elevation frame, supported by a common antenna support, or otherwise positioned such that movement of the elevation frame adjusts the pointing direction of at least one of the antennas. The antennas may be configured for communication with different satellites, networks, frequency bands, polarizations, or communication channels.

A controller is operatively connected to the first, second, and third drive mechanisms. The controller may receive signals from one or more sensors configured to sense motion, angular position, angular velocity, acceleration, tilt, roll, pitch, yaw, or displacement associated with the base, the vertical support, the level frame, the elevation frame, or one or more of the axes. Based at least in part on the sensed motion, the controller may command the first drive mechanism, the second drive mechanism, and/or the third drive mechanism to adjust the orientation of the antenna mount.

The controller may also be configured to select one of the first and second antennas for active use. Selection may be based on signal strength, signal quality, target direction, satellite availability, communication requirements, obstruction detection, frequency band, polarization, or other operational criteria. After selecting an antenna, the controller may adjust the position of the antenna mount to maintain or improve alignment of the selected antenna with a desired target, such as a satellite, terrestrial transmitter, receiver, or communication node.

---

## Example Claims

### Claim 1  
An antenna mounting system comprising:  
a base;  
a vertical support rotatably coupled to the base;  
a first drive operatively coupled to the vertical support and configured to rotate the vertical support relative to the base about a first axis;  
a level frame pivotably coupled to the vertical support;  
a second drive operatively coupled to the level frame and configured to pivot the level frame relative to the vertical support about a second axis;  
an elevation frame pivotably coupled to the level frame;  
a third drive operatively coupled to the elevation frame and configured to pivot the elevation frame relative to the level frame about a third axis;  
a first antenna and a second antenna supported by the antenna mounting system; and  
a controller operatively coupled to the first drive, the second drive, and the third drive, the controller being configured to select one of the first antenna and the second antenna and to control at least one of the first drive, the second drive, and the third drive based at least in part on sensed motion associated with at least one of the first axis, the second axis, and the third axis.

### Claim 2  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the first axis is an azimuth axis.

### Claim 3  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the second axis is a leveling axis.

### Claim 4  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the third axis is an elevation axis.

### Claim 5  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, further comprising at least one sensor configured to generate a signal indicative of angular motion associated with one or more of the vertical support, the level frame, and the elevation frame.

### Claim 6  
The antenna mounting system of claim 5, wherein the at least one sensor comprises at least one of an accelerometer, a gyroscope, an inclinometer, an encoder, or an inertial measurement unit.

### Claim 7  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to control the first drive, the second drive, and the third drive to maintain alignment of the selected antenna with a communication target.

### Claim 8  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the first antenna and the second antenna are mounted to the elevation frame.

### Claim 9  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to select between the first antenna and the second antenna based at least in part on signal quality.

### Claim 10  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to adjust a position of the elevation frame based on sensed angular displacement of the level frame.

### Claim 11  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the first drive, the second drive, and the third drive each comprise an electric motor.

### Claim 12  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to compensate for motion of a platform to which the base is mounted.

### Claim 13  
The antenna mounting system of claim 12, wherein the platform comprises a vehicle, marine vessel, aircraft, or movable structure.

### Claim 14  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the first antenna and the second antenna are configured to operate in different frequency bands.

### Claim 15  
The antenna mounting system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to command the first drive to adjust azimuth, command the second drive to adjust level orientation, and command the third drive to adjust elevation.

---

## Alternative Independent Claim

An apparatus for positioning a selected antenna, the apparatus comprising:  
a base;  
a first frame rotatable relative to the base about an azimuth axis;  
a second frame pivotable relative to the first frame about a leveling axis;  
a third frame pivotable relative to the second frame about an elevation axis;  
a first actuator configured to rotate the first frame about the azimuth axis;  
a second actuator configured to pivot the second frame about the leveling axis;  
a third actuator configured to pivot the third frame about the elevation axis;  
a plurality of antennas including at least a first antenna and a second antenna;  
one or more sensors configured to sense motion associated with at least one of the azimuth axis, the leveling axis, and the elevation axis; and  
a controller configured to select one antenna from the plurality of antennas and to control the first actuator, the second actuator, and the third actuator in response to the sensed motion to position the selected antenna.

A system comprises an antenna support platform configured to position one or more antennas with respect to at least three axes of motion. The antenna support platform includes an azimuth drive configured to rotate the platform about an azimuth axis, a leveling drive configured to adjust a level frame relative to a base or support structure, and an elevation drive configured to adjust an elevation angle of an antenna support relative to the level frame.

In one embodiment, first and second antennas are mounted to the level frame or to an antenna support carried by the level frame. The first and second antennas may be arranged to maintain a predetermined spatial relationship while being positioned by the azimuth, leveling, and elevation drives. The antennas may be configured for transmitting, receiving, or both transmitting and receiving electromagnetic signals.

The system further includes a plurality of sensors associated with the respective axes of motion. An azimuth sensor is configured to generate azimuth position data representative of an angular position of the platform about the azimuth axis. A leveling sensor is configured to generate leveling position data representative of an orientation or tilt of the level frame. An elevation sensor is configured to generate elevation position data representative of an angular position of the antenna support or antennas about an elevation axis.

A control unit is operatively coupled to the azimuth drive, the leveling drive, the elevation drive, and the plurality of sensors. The control unit is configured to receive the azimuth position data, the leveling position data, and the elevation position data, and to determine a current position and orientation of the level frame and the antennas based at least in part on the received sensor data. The control unit is further configured to generate and output drive commands to at least one of the azimuth drive, the leveling drive, and the elevation drive to move the level frame and the antennas toward a desired position or orientation.

In certain implementations, the control unit may execute a closed-loop control process in which sensor feedback from the azimuth, leveling, and elevation sensors is used to command the corresponding drives. The control unit may thereby coordinate azimuth rotation, leveling adjustment, and elevation positioning to maintain or acquire a selected pointing direction for the first and second antennas.
